gen-dafont-dogica-gf-orienta: Orienta reads as modern and hollow-cheeked, its counters breathing with barely any gap between upper and lower case. And Dogica above it is the opposite: heavy, wide-tracked, with lowercase crowding the capitals, so a long page of plain sans text would feel like a quiet room after a shout.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-oxygen:
Oxygen reads clean and contemporary, with curves that never quite close up.

Dogica is the one to lean on for weight and wide-spaced command, while Oxygen does the steady work of carrying sentences with lowercase nearly as tall as its capitals.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-parkinsans: Modern and crisp, Parkinsans keeps one stroke thickness throughout, and its wide-mouthed letters hold up even when shrunk. But Dogica does what it does best at the top, heavy and wide-tracked, while the sans-serif body simply keeps every word at the same weight.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-pathway-extreme: Dogica leads with a wide, heavy stance, its lowercase rising close to capitals and each curve left open at the end. Pathway Extreme follows with stubby stems and a big x-height.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-preahvihear: Dogica's lowercase climbs nearly to the height of its capitals, spaced wide and weighty, a blunt, commanding look. And Preahvihear, a contemporary sans-serif with a lofty x-height and mouths pried wide open, would carry a long passage with ease.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-prompt: Wide tracking and heavy, commanding lowercase that nearly matches its capitals make Dogica unmistakable at the top. Prompt, a plain sans with oversized small letters, settles in beneath.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-pt-sans-caption: Blunt, heavy and wide-spaced, Dogica hits hard, its curves left open at their ends. PT Sans Caption, a big-bodied sans-serif with inviting bowls, fills in below.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-puritan:
Puritan reads clean and friendly, with rounded forms open to the side.

And Dogica, heavy and wide-tracked above it, makes a long stretch of that sans feel easy, since the oversized e and a counters keep every line approachable.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-questrial:
Dogica comes in heavy and wide, lowercase rising near its capitals.

Questrial, a modern sans-serif, is the better one for flat, single-weight strokes with no shift from heavy to light, while Dogica does the commanding work of announcing the page.
gen-dafont-dogica-gf-radio-canada:
Radio Canada draws a steady line, like blueprint lettering.

Its tall, full c, s and z and the clear openings at curve ends give the sans a precise clarity, and Dogica's heavy, wide-tracked weight above it makes that difference the pair's strongest quality.
